findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, and no ACL is set, so this bucket stores objects (including the seeded vendor-roster.xlsx) without enforced encryption at rest, and relies on AWS default private ACL which is fragile.
The bucket has acl = private but no server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning ledger export data is stored unencrypted at rest despite being sensitive financial data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, leaving operational runbooks (which may contain sensitive operational details) unencrypted at rest.

The acl attribute is set to the malformed/non-standard value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' instead of a valid canned ACL like 'log-delivery-write-only' or 'private'. This is likely a typo that could cause apply-time failure or, if it resolves to an unintended canned ACL, could grant unintended read/write access to the audit trail bucket, undermining the integrity of audit logs.

This object is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.reports_archive, which has no server-side encryption configured, so the vendor-roster.xlsx file (potentially containing sensitive vendor data) is stored in cleartext at rest.
